newsitem.title: USA: US spot resid prices gain with crude, gas, weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot resid prices gain with crude, gas, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly edged higher Monday in lackluster trade, helped by sharp rallies in crude and natgas and forecasts for much colder East Coast weather later in the week, sources said.
"Resid was talked higher because of crude, gas and the (cold) weather, but not much happened," said one cash trader, adding sellers were holding out, waiting for the season's first Arctic blast.
New York Harbor one pct edged up slightly to $21.75-22.00 a barrel, with January paper early talked 25-50 cents higher at $21.75-22.00 but pegged closer to $22.75 later with crude.
High sulphurs in New York were steady to up slightly, with 2.2 percent pegged a quarter higher at about $18.50.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour gained 25 cents to about the $23.00 level, traders said.
U.S. Gulf Coast one percent was unchanged at $18.50, while three percent notionally firmed a quarter to $16.00-25.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate gas prices firmed 30-40 cents Monday to the $4.40/mmBtu area compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.47/mmBtu equivalent. For January, New York gas traded at $1.70 over the screen, or in the high-$5.00/mmBtu area, well-above resid paper at a $3.60/mmBtu equivalent.
